results.text: Skip to content Register Sign In Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live World LIVE Clashes erupt in Paris and other cities after thousands join mostly peaceful protests across France There has not yet been a repeat of the chaos seen during previous protests, our correspondent in Paris reports. Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits The slowed Starlink connections had affected the Ukraine's military and drone operations for a week. 5 hrs ago Europe Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer. 3 hrs ago US & Canada Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say. 8 hrs ago Europe Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany. 2 hrs ago Europe Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher. 19 hrs ago US & Canada British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas Nathan Gregory says the loss of childhood sweetheart Leanne "is unimaginable for our family". 19 mins ago Nottinghamshire Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack The independent MP is now in a serious but stable condition, according to the Melbourne hospital. Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule. White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets. Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction. WATCH/LISTEN Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man following the fire. Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink? President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it. Doctors tell the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals by paramilitary fighters A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system. Blue Planet III: Moment octopus escapes death after hunt gone wrong The sequence is part of the latest Blue Planet series from Sir David Attenborough. 'It's part of the culture' - New York bans horse-drawn carriages after more than 160 years The BBC's Madeline Halpert spoke to city tourists, residents and horse carriage workers about the industry and their opinion on the ban. MORE TO EXPLORE The rise of AI election ads in US midterms campaign BBC Verify has tracked dozens of AI ads to assess how they are being used by campaigns in the midterms. 12 hrs ago BBC Verify How Brazil's changing working class is reshaping the presidential race Calls for change present a challenge to President Lula in the second round of the election on Sunday. 12 hrs ago Latin America Hispanic voters helped bring Trump to power - in Texas, the tide may be turning Recent polls
